maggie: Quick heads-up — spun up a mini bring-up of Llama3-12B q4f16 with our early-exit speculative sampler (spec_rate=0.7, fallback_p=0.05) on the canary pool. Observed ~1.9x throughput vs baseline and ~18% improvement p50 latency, but a non-trivial quality delta on our dev holdouts. Sharing numbers and short logs below.

akshay: Can you paste the eval protocol + metrics? curious whether it's a metric shift (EM/ROUGE) or increased randomness.

lena: Short paste from the eval run (dev-holdout subset, 2k examples, deterministic prompts):

Metrics summary:
- baseline (fp16, no-spec): EM 78.6 | ROUGE-L 64.2 | avg_prob_repeats 0.8%
- q4f16 (no-spec): EM 77.9 | ROUGE-L 63.8 | avg_prob_repeats 0.9%
- q4f16 + speculative (spec_rate=0.7, fallback_p=0.05): EM 75.2 | ROUGE-L 61.1 | avg_prob_repeats 1.7%

Worth noting: the biggest regression is on short-answer extraction (SQuAD-like). Generated outputs include truncated spans or repeated trailing tokens in ~0.6% of cases.

rick: Do we have logs showing when fallback triggered? could be that fallback is too rare and early-exit returns low-confidence tokens.

lena: yes — pasted a condensed log excerpt below:

[eval-bot] 2026-03-20T14:12:23Z canary-run id=jj-420 spec_tick=0.7 fallback_p=0.05 batch=16
[model] example=1423 start=0 speculative_path=true early_accept=true token_conf=0.22 -> returned token 'the' (truncated)
[model] example=1423 fallback=true restart_seq=true
[model] example=1587 speculative_path=true early_accept=false fallback=false token_conf=0.81 -> continued ok

lena: the token_conf histogram is shifted lower on q4 runs; seems quantized logits compress tails, so speculative decision boundary needs recalibration.

maggie: Good catch. Hypothesis: quantization increases uncertainty under speculative policy, causing premature accepts. Two immediate experiments: 1) raise fallback_p to 0.12 and lower spec_rate to 0.55; 2) add a small logit-temperature fix on the spec decision (temp=0.9) to spread probs.

akshay: Also try enabling prefix-KV warmup (force_kv_warmup=true) on first few tokens — we saw benefit on long context cases last year. Could reduce those truncated starts.

lena: I'll queue three runs (A/B/C):
A: q4f16 spec_rate=0.55 fallback_p=0.12 temp_spec=1.0 kv_warmup=false
B: q4f16 spec_rate=0.7 fallback_p=0.05 temp_spec=0.9 kv_warmup=true
C: q4f16 spec_rate=0.7 fallback_p=0.05 temp_spec=1.0 kv_warmup=true + run with eval-tool fuzzed prompts (+typos)

Command I'm using to launch eval harness (internal):
```
./infra/run_eval.sh --model llama3-12b-q4f16 --spec-rate 0.7 --fallback 0.05 --batch 16 --seed 42 --dataset dev_holdout_2k --tag canary-239876
```

ci-bot: scheduled job canary-239876: queued -> running on pool-canary-3 (GPU A100-80G)

maggie: Add a small automated regression check: fail if EM drops >1.5 pts vs baseline or hallucination-class >0.5% increase. If failed, auto-create a rollback task for the canary.

eval-bot: run complete (canary-239876). Summary attached to thread: http://internal/eval/canary-239876 (internal link)

akshay: If A/B shows C improves robustness on fuzzed prompts, we should consider codifying kv_warmup + slightly higher fallback as a default profile for q4 quantized models when spec is enabled.

lena: Will share raw logs & per-example diffs in the eval artifact. Quick note: when spec_rate low (<=0.4) we lose most perf wins; there's a narrow sweet spot.

rick: Thanks — once the three runs finish, can you spike an adversarial subset (edge-case NER + short-span answers) and push to canary-extended? I want to eyeball failure modes.

maggie: agreed. Also let's add a small probe to record top-5 logits distribution before spec decision. That will help tune the threshold without relying purely on end-to-end metrics.

akshay: ack — sounds like a solid plan. ping me when results in eval dashboard. :eyes: 

maggie: thanks team — will follow up with results thread and recommended rollout params. :thumbsup:
